text:
Naveen: Dropping a refreshed mock for the API Keys page. Focus today: the create/rotate/revoke flows, empty states, and keyboard/a11y touches. Figma: https://figma.com/...

Kara: Quick skim 1: love the compact list. Two immediate questions: where does the secret show up after create, and how do we prevent accidental revoke?

Priya: For create, we were thinking of a one-time reveal card (modal) that shows the secret with a copy button + reminder to store it. No auto-copy.

Omar: Modal is fine. Make sure the modal traps focus and that the copy button has aria-label like "Copy secret for <key-name>". Also consider allowing users to download a CSV for multiple keys.

Naveen: Good call on CSV. We'll add an export action on the top-right. Regarding revoke, current pattern is: kebab -> Revoke -> confirm by typing key name. Is that too heavy for user-scoped keys?

Kara: Typing name is strong for org-level or admin keys. For personal keys, maybe checkbox + type "REVOKE"? That feels gimmicky. I prefer checkbox + confirm for personal, name typing for org/global.

Priya: Agree. Let's make the confirmation modal adaptive: shows typing field for keys with "sensitive" flag set in metadata. Other keys get a checkbox and a short sentence: "This cannot be undone."

a11y-bot: Suggestion: confirmation fields must be labeled and announced. Provide aria-describedby linking to the irreversible-warning text. Also ensure the modal has role="dialog" and aria-modal="true".

Omar: Accessibility aside, copy for rotate modal needs clarity. Current copy: "Rotate key? A new key will be issued." We should state whether old key is immediately invalid or has a grace period.

Kara: Proposal copy:

"Rotate API key?
A new key will be created immediately. The previous key will stop accepting requests after 2 minutes to allow short transition windows. Update your integrations before the window ends."

Priya: I like that. Add a link to the migration checklist and mention webhook retries if applicable.

Naveen: On the list UI: do we show full scope names inline or condensed chips with a "+n" when there are many? Chips make the row tall.

Omar: Use condensed chips with a visually hidden text that screen readers read out full scope list. The visible UI shows "3 scopes" with a button to expand. Expanded view uses pills.

a11y-bot: Make sure the expand button has aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to the expanded content. When expanded, focus should move into the expansion region.

Kara: Keyboard flow nit: current tab order in prototype is checkbox -> name -> created -> scopes -> actions. Suggest changing to checkbox -> name -> scopes -> created -> actions so screen reader users get context about scopes before actions.

Priya: Agreed. We'll reorder DOM accordingly. Also, avoid putting interactive tooltips before main content; tooltips should be triggered from the control not be in the tab order.

Naveen: Secret reveal in toasts is risky. We should avoid ephemeral toasts for secrets. Modal reveal with optional copy sounds better and safer. Also ensure there's no auto-dismiss when secret shown.

Omar: Regarding the action layout: should Rotate be an inline text button or only in the kebab? If inline, it increases width and misclick risk.

Kara: If Rotate is common, keep inline but ghost style (low visual weight). Add a small confirm step and an undo toast for 30 seconds that can re-enable the old key for admins. That adds complexity. Maybe simpler: rotate modal shows countdown and link to revoke immediately if needed.

Priya: Undo toast is nice but let's avoid adding rollback complexity in this iteration. Keep rotate modal with migration window and clear docs link.

a11y-bot: For the kebab menu ensure it is keyboard operable: open via Enter/Space, navigate items with Arrow keys, Escape closes. Announce menu role as menu and items as menuitem. Add aria-labels to include key name: "Rotate key: <key-name>".

Naveen: Empty state copy currently "No keys". Change to: "You haven't created any API keys yet 1 Create an API key to start integrating with Redwood Inference." Primary CTA "Create API key"; secondary link "Key best practices". Add a small permission hint if user lacks create rights: "Request key creation" link.

Kara: For mobile/smaller screens, collapse the table into card rows where actions live in a footer area. Ensure actions are reachable by screen readers and not hidden behind hover states.

Priya: Test plan: I'll add keyboard and VoiceOver test cases (tab order, modal labeling, kebab navigation, secret reveal flow) and edge-case tests for very long scope lists.

Omar: I'll update the Figma with these changes: adaptive revoke confirmation, rotate copy with 2-minute window, modal secret reveal, reordered tab sequence, and CSV export action.

Naveen: Great. If no objections I'll push copy changes and a11y checklist to the ticket later today. :thumbsup:

Kara: No objections. Priya, ping me when tests are ready.

Priya: Will do.

a11y-bot: Reminder: run axe-core on the component story after updates.

Naveen: Thanks all 1 closing thread once Figma updated.
